steps.title: Miqat Preparation and Intention for Qiran
steps.instructions: Prepare for Hajj and Umrah combined by performing ritual cleansing (ghusl), trimming nails, and donning the ihram garments (two unstitched white sheets for men; modest clothing for women). Formulate the intention (niyyah) in your heart for performing Hajj and Umrah concurrently (Qiran). Recite the Talbiya repeatedly.
steps.location_context: At the appointed Miqat station corresponding to your direction of travel before entering the Haram boundary.
steps.adab: Maintain humility, increase remembrance of Allah, and avoid arguments or harsh speech.
steps.dua: Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka wa al-mulk, la sharika lak.
steps.safety_notes: Ensure hydration before entering ihram. Elderly users should wear comfortable sandals to prevent blisters.
steps.image_prompt: An educational diagram showing a pilgrim at the Miqat station wearing ihram garments, with directional arrows indicating entry into the sacred boundary.
steps.image_caption: Preparing at the Miqat station for Qiran.
steps.image_alt_text: Diagram of a pilgrim in ihram at the Miqat boundary.

steps.title: Arrival in Makkah and Tawaf al-Qudum
steps.instructions: Upon reaching Makkah, proceed to the Grand Mosque (Masjid al-Haram). Perform the Arrival Tawaf (Tawaf al-Qudum) by circling the Kaaba seven times counter-clockwise, starting and ending at the Black Stone corner. Note: Scholars differ on whether Tawaf al-Qudum is strictly required or strongly recommended for Qiran pilgrims.
steps.location_context: Mataf area surrounding the Kaaba inside Masjid al-Haram, Makkah.
steps.adab: Keep your gaze lowered respectfully, avoid pushing others, and move calmly.
steps.safety_notes: Crowds can be dense. Elderly and first-time users should utilize designated upper levels or wheelchair assistance lanes if mobility is limited.
steps.image_prompt: A clear, respectful vector illustration of the Mataf area showing pilgrims circling the Kaaba in concentric paths.
steps.image_caption: Performing Tawaf al-Qudum around the Kaaba.
steps.image_alt_text: Illustration showing pilgrims performing Tawaf around the Kaaba.

steps.title: Sa'i for Hajj and Umrah Combined
steps.instructions: After completing Tawaf, walk seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwa. Because this is Hajj Qiran, a single Sa'i suffices for both the Umrah and Hajj components according to the majority view.
steps.location_context: Mas'a gallery connecting Safa and Marwa inside Masjid al-Haram.
steps.adab: Walk at a steady pace, run lightly only in the designated green-lighted zone if physically able.
steps.safety_notes: The distance is approximately 3.5 kilometers total. Pace yourself, take rest breaks, and stay hydrated using available Zamzam water stations.
steps.image_prompt: An architectural cross-section diagram of the Mas'a corridor showing the path between Safa and Marwa.
steps.image_caption: Walking between Safa and Marwa for Sa'i.
steps.image_alt_text: Diagram illustrating the path of Sa'i between Safa and Marwa.

steps.title: Remaining in Ihram and Tarwiyah Day at Mina
steps.instructions: Unlike Tamattu', a Qiran pilgrim remains in ihram after Sa'i and does not exit it. On the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah (Day of Tarwiyah), proceed to Mina and offer the five daily prayers (Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and Fajr of Arafah) shortening them without combining.
steps.adab: Engage in personal reflection, Quran recitation, and quiet supplication.
steps.safety_notes: Ensure you stay within your assigned camp sector in Mina. Keep your emergency contact badge visible.
steps.image_prompt: An organized map graphic showing the tent encampments of Mina with directional markers.
steps.image_caption: Staying in Mina during the Day of Tarwiyah.
steps.image_alt_text: Map graphic of Mina tent camps.

steps.title: Standing at Arafah
steps.instructions: After sunrise on the 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah, move to the plain of Arafah. Remain within the boundaries of Arafah until sunset, engaging in continuous prayer, remembrance, and repentance. Combine and shorten Dhuhr and Asr prayers at Masjid Namira or your camp.
steps.location_context: Plain of Arafah and Jabal al-Rahmah.
steps.adab: Face the Qiblah, raise hands in earnest supplication, and maintain patience despite heat and crowds.
steps.safety_notes: Heat exhaustion is a major risk. Use umbrellas, drink plenty of oral rehydration solutions, and remain inside cooled tents during peak afternoon hours.
steps.image_prompt: An educational safety graphic highlighting hydration and sun protection in Arafah.
steps.image_caption: Supplicating on the plain of Arafah.
steps.image_alt_text: Safety and guidance graphic for the Day of Arafah.

steps.title: Muzdalifah Overnight Stay and Pebble Collection
steps.instructions: After sunset on the 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah, depart Arafah for Muzdalifah without praying Maghrib on the way. Upon arrival, combine and pray Maghrib and Isha. Spend the night under the open sky and collect pebbles for the stoning ritual.
steps.adab: Rest quietly and prepare spiritually for the rituals of the following day.
steps.safety_notes: Muzdalifah can be extremely crowded at night. Stay close to your group leader and avoid sleeping near main pedestrian pathways.
steps.image_prompt: A clear night-sky iconographic map showing pilgrims resting in Muzdalifah.
steps.image_caption: Overnight stay and pebble collection in Muzdalifah.
steps.image_alt_text: Map illustration of Muzdalifah overnight stay.

steps.title: Rami al-Jamarat (Stoning the Big Pillar) on Eid al-Adha
steps.instructions: After Fajr in Muzdalifah, proceed to Mina before sunrise. Go to Jamrat al-Aqba (the largest pillar) and throw seven small pebbles consecutively, saying 'Bismillahi Allahu Akbar' with each throw.
steps.adab: Maintain calm and composure; avoid throwing large objects or shoes.
steps.safety_notes: Follow designated crowd-flow schedules provided by authorities. Elderly and vulnerable pilgrims should delegate the stoning to a trusted proxy if peak hours pose physical risks.
steps.image_prompt: A safety diagram illustrating the correct method of holding and tossing small pebbles at the Jamarat pillar.
steps.image_caption: Stoning Jamrat al-Aqba on Eid day.
steps.image_alt_text: Diagram showing how to perform Rami at the Jamarat.

steps.title: Animal Sacrifice (Hady) for Qiran
steps.instructions: Because Qiran mandates an animal sacrifice, arrange for the slaughter of your Hady (sacrifice). Note: Many pilgrims purchase official vouchers through authorized Islamic banking channels to fulfill this requirement safely.
steps.location_context: Slaughterhouse zones in Mina or Makkah abattoirs.
steps.adab: Express gratitude to Allah for the provisions and facilitate distribution to those in need.
steps.safety_notes: Do not attempt to enter active industrial slaughter areas yourself unless authorized; use official distribution systems.
steps.image_prompt: An infographic illustrating the authorized Hady voucher and distribution process.
steps.image_alt_text: Infographic showing the animal sacrifice process for Qiran.

steps.title: First Halq or Taqseer (Shaving or Trimming Hair)
steps.instructions: After the sacrifice, men must shave their heads (halq) or shorten their hair (taqseer); women trim a fingertip-length portion of their hair. This marks the first release from ihram restrictions (Halal al-Awwal), permitting normal clothing and perfume, excluding marital relations.
steps.adab: Use clean, sterile blades if shaving personally or visit licensed barbers.
steps.safety_notes: Avoid unsterilized shared razor blades at unofficial street stalls to prevent blood-borne infections.
steps.image_prompt: A sanitary guidelines icon set showing sterile single-use razors for hair trimming.
steps.image_caption: Shaving or trimming hair after sacrifice.
steps.image_alt_text: Icons demonstrating safe hair trimming practices.

steps.title: Tawaf al-Ifadah and Sa'i Completion
steps.instructions: Proceed to the Grand Mosque in Makkah to perform Tawaf al-Ifadah (the essential Tawaf of Hajj). Since you performed Sa'i earlier upon arrival in Qiran, scholarly opinions differ on whether a second Sa'i is needed; many traditional schools hold that the initial Sa'i suffices for Qiran.
steps.adab: Perform prayers and drink Zamzam water upon completion.
steps.safety_notes: Tawaf al-Ifadah can experience extreme congestion on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah. Plan travel times carefully.
steps.image_prompt: A top-down architectural diagram of Masjid al-Haram indicating Tawaf al-Ifadah flow routes.
steps.image_alt_text: Diagram showing Tawaf al-Ifadah routes in the Haram.

steps.title: Ayyam al-Tashreeq: Stoning and Overnight Stays in Mina
steps.instructions: Return to Mina to spend the nights of the 11th, 12th (and optionally 13th) of Dhu al-Hijjah. Each afternoon after midday, stone all three Jamarat pillars (Small, Middle, and Large) using seven pebbles for each pillar in sequence.
steps.location_context: Mina tent camps and Jamarat Bridge.
steps.adab: Patience, remembrance of Allah, and courteous behavior toward fellow pilgrims.
steps.safety_notes: Adhere strictly to designated camp evacuation routes and schedules for stoning provided by camp administrators.
steps.image_prompt: A sequential diagram showing the order of stoning the three Jamarat pillars during Tashreeq days.
steps.image_caption: Stoning the three pillars during Tashreeq days.
steps.image_alt_text: Diagram illustrating the sequence for stoning the three Jamarat.

steps.title: Farewell Tawaf (Tawaf al-Wada')
steps.instructions: Before departing Makkah permanently, perform the Farewell Tawaf (Tawaf al-Wada') by circling the Kaaba seven times. This must be the absolute final act of your pilgrimage before leaving the city boundary.
steps.adab: Depart with a tearful heart, expressing gratitude and praying for an accepted Hajj.
steps.safety_notes: Allow ample time for travel arrangements. If delayed after Tawaf al-Wada' due to unforeseen circumstances, scholarly consensus generally requires repeating the Tawaf.
steps.image_prompt: An inspirational illustration depicting a pilgrim looking back at the Kaaba during departure.
steps.image_caption: Performing the Farewell Tawaf before departure.
steps.image_alt_text: Illustration showing a pilgrim during Tawaf al-Wada'.
